input.text: Off the streets south of Tiananmen hides a perfect wooden opera house from imperial times: Huguang Guild Hall. Guild halls were hometown clubs for merchants and scholars away from home — this one served merchants from Hubei and Hunan, founded in eighteen oh seven — and its courtyard stage hosted the greatest names of Peking opera's golden age; the acoustics of its all-wood, nail-free structure were part of the show. Today the hall is the Beijing Opera Museum — costumes, scripts, masks, and the stories of the art's two-century rise — and its stage still performs: on scheduled evenings, real Peking opera plays here to a modest, lucky audience. For first-timers, this small hall beats the grand theaters: every seat close, every gesture visible, tea served as it was a century ago. Combine with the nearby Liulichang cultural street for one old-Peking evening. The dynasty is gone; the show, happily, is not.
